verdict.rationale: The evidence makes the charter holder clear: Column N.A. describes itself as a nationally chartered bank, a Column engineer calls it an issuing bank, and accounts are opened as FDIC-insured accounts at Column itself, so there is no partner-bank or middleware layer. What happens to customers if the platform fails is only implied by the FDIC-insured label, with no documented failure, resolution or pass-through insurance treatment for FBO end customers. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of customer outcomes on platform or bank failure, pass-through FDIC coverage for FBO/end-customer funds, and independent corroboration of the charter status.

support.subject: As a founder, I know exactly who holds the charter — whether the platform is a bank, a direct program with a named partner bank, or middleware between me and someone else's sponsor — and what happens to my customers if the platform fails

citations.quote: Column N.A. is the first nationally chartered bank created to serve developers and builders
Programmatically open and manage FDIC insured bank accounts at Column on behalf of your customers.
We're an issuing bank and sponsor card programs on Visa & Mastercard.
